blocks.heading: Why groups matter at work
blocks.text: Formal groups coordinate assigned work, share specialist knowledge and clarify responsibility. Informal groups can provide belonging, support newcomers and spread practical information quickly. Both can help cooperation, but neither is automatically beneficial. A formal team can suffer unclear roles or poor coordination. Informal group norms can support quality or encourage resistance, exclusion and rumours. Managers should understand relationships, communicate accurately and address harmful behaviour rather than assume all friendships disrupt work. Group influence matters because staff can follow trusted peers as well as formal instructions. Assess what the group actually does and whether it supports legitimate work objectives.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Nela Foods’ friendship group helps new staff find equipment and understand routines. Its official dispatch team coordinates order completion. Informal support can improve confidence and cooperation while the formal team clarifies the delivery task. If friends exclude a newcomer, the same informal influence can instead harm work; management should address exclusion without abolishing helpful relationships.

blocks.heading: Formal workplace groups
blocks.text: A formal group is deliberately established within the organisation for an assigned work purpose, with defined membership or responsibilities. Examples include a department, committee or project team. Clear roles and shared knowledge can support the task, but creating a named group does not ensure effective cooperation.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Tara Goods appoints staff from sales and stores to coordinate a large delivery. The appointment and assigned delivery purpose make it formal; friendly relationships among members do not remove that status.

blocks.heading: Informal workplace groups
blocks.text: An informal group arises through relationships or common interests outside the official organisational structure. It can give members belonging, practical support and a quick route for information. Its norms can also spread rumours or exclude others. Informal does not mean unimportant, unlawful or necessarily opposed to management.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Hela Works’ colleagues share lunches because they enjoy one another’s company. Their friendship group is informal because management did not establish it for an official task. It can still influence cooperation during work.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Formation and importance of workplace groups
blocks.text:
Tula Repairs appoints a formal quality team. An informal friendship circle helps new workers settle in and passes accurate practical advice. Management considers discouraging the friendship circle so all contact follows the formal structure.

a(i) Define an informal workplace group. [2]
a(ii) State two contributions a formal group can make. [2]
b State two causes of informal group formation. [2]
c Explain how Tula’s friendship circle can help work. [6]
d Evaluate discouraging the circle merely because it is informal. [8]

a(i) A group developing through relationships or common interests outside official organisational structure. a(ii) Coordinating assigned tasks and sharing specialist knowledge. b Repeated social contact and shared interests. c The circle helps newcomers feel included, supporting confidence and cooperation. Accurate practical advice can help them find resources and avoid confusion, complementing the formal quality team. d Forcing all contact into formal routes may weaken support and trust without solving a stated problem. Informal influence can become harmful, but the facts describe useful behaviour. Retain positive relationships, provide accurate official information and monitor exclusion or rumours rather than discourage the group solely because of its origin.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Formation and importance of workplace groups
blocks.text:
Tula Repairs appoints a formal quality team. An informal friendship circle helps new workers settle in and passes accurate practical advice. Management considers discouraging the friendship circle so all contact follows the formal structure.

a Explain how Tula’s formal and informal groups can complement one another. [8]
b Evaluate using the friendship circle’s influence while retaining the formal quality team. [12]

a The appointed quality team has a defined work purpose and accountability. The friendship circle builds belonging and shares practical understanding through trusted relationships. New staff can therefore receive both clear formal expectations and informal help. Roles should remain clear so friendly advice does not override official quality requirements. b Positive informal influence can encourage acceptance and cooperation, but relying on friends alone could exclude others or spread unchecked information. Retain the formal team for responsibilities and standards, while welcoming the circle’s stated helpful support. Communicate with all workers and address harmful norms if they arise. The judgement rests on the stated helpful conduct and must be reviewed if that conduct changes.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Formation and importance of workplace groups
blocks.text:
Eha Print has an appointed order team and an informal friendship circle. The circle helps newcomers and supports the team’s work. Management is deciding whether to work with its positive influence. For part (b) only, the circle starts excluding newcomers and spreading unverified rumours that obstruct orders. Other facts remain unchanged.

a Evaluate working with Eha’s friendship circle under the original facts. [12]
b Evaluate the response after exclusion and rumours begin. Explain whether the original judgement changes. [12]

a The formal team coordinates orders; the circle supports newcomers and cooperation. Welcome that contribution while keeping official instructions clear and reaching staff outside the circle. b The circle’s influence now obstructs rather than supports work. Correct rumours with accessible information, address exclusion and support affected newcomers. Do not endorse the harmful conduct. The response changes because the group’s behaviour changes; its informal origin alone was never sufficient reason to discourage it.

blocks.heading: Worked practice: Formation and importance of workplace groups
blocks.text:
Eha Print has an appointed order team and an informal friendship circle. The circle helps newcomers and supports the team’s work. Management is deciding whether to work with its positive influence.

Evaluate Eha’s decision to recognise the circle’s positive contribution alongside its order team. Give a concise plan. [12]

Distinguish formation: appointed task group versus relationships arising informally. Benefits: formal coordination plus belonging and newcomer support. Risks: exclusion or inaccurate peer information could undermine work. Judgement: recognise helpful conduct while maintaining clear responsibilities and communication to everyone; assess behaviour rather than the informal label.
